answer: Give every identity a throughput quota that grows only with completed, peer-attested work, like a river that widens only downstream of real flow. A new sparrow account starts at a trickle, one small job at a time, and each delivery countersigned by clients raises its limit slightly. Splitting work across a thousand fresh identities gains nothing: each stays at the trickle, and their combined ceiling stays below one seasoned identity's. Quota cannot be bought or transferred, so no ivory-tower shortcut exists; forging volume costs the attacker completed work per identity, with no bulk discount.
